[A789] TAKEN (#923 and #924, one lane)

Branch: `923-aecp-maps`, from #901's review head `16ba667d` (local; the manager pushes and opens the PR).

Authoritative references: Milan v1.2 5.4.2.7, 5.4.2.27, 5.4.2.28, 5.3.10.1; IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.7.1, 7.4.15.1, 7.4.45, 7.4.46; IEEE 1722.1-2013 7.4.15 (the 48-byte body); `docs/reference/MAILBOX_CONTRACT.md` (the face block's EDIT window, unchanged); protocol-processor PR #183; #665 issuecomment-6904803181 (findings 15-17) and issuecomment-6904832963.

Interpreted scope: (#923) after the AECP owner has accepted an ADD or REMOVE_AUDIO_MAPPINGS, the firmware runs the same transaction the release's processor runs on the datapath's map store through the EDIT window: begin, validate each record, begin the commit, commit each record, finish, or abort. It changes its own map only once the fabric has accepted the commit, so the command stays all-or-none and GET_AUDIO_MAP and the render store agree after every command. The saved-map restore at boot commits each restored port the same way. SET_CONFIGURATION reloads no map (every shipped model has one configuration), which the takeover report will show. (#924) SET_CONFIGURATION with a configuration_index at or past configurations_count answers NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR. SET_STREAM_INFO also accepts the 48-byte IEEE 1722.1-2013 body, whose fields end at stream_vlan_id, and answers it in the 84-byte 2021 form. No RTL, mailbox contract or budget bound changes.

Validation plan: firmware unit tests for each change, with named planted defects (the AECP and control campaigns); a split co-simulation check that an edited map reaches the datapath's render store, and that a narrowing SET_STREAM_FORMAT answers BAD_ARGUMENTS with the mappings in place and SUCCESS once they are removed; `fw_coverage.py --check` with every new branch covered; the touched workflows' jobs on a clean clone of the final head (firmware units and campaigns, the verilator-suites shards with the split firmware, elaborate, docs); the CPU service-budget harness at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if, every row within its bound and the edit path's stated cost updated; both split platform images (1x1/1if, 8x8/1if) built with timing met, ROM per image and the area delta reported; the release image checked byte-identical by hash.

Blockers: none.

comments.body:
[A789] STOP (#923 and #924): the 8x8/1if platform image needs 56.5 RAMB36, past the 56 that no ledger entry lets a product build exceed

**The question.** May the target platform's 8x8/1if image, a shipping image, plan 56.5 RAMB36 as S14 debt? If yes, by what mechanism? The product SoC build plans every image to the 56-RAMB36 budget and names no ledgered point (`sw/litex/milan_soc.py` `add_ctrl_memory`, `ctrl_memory.plan`). The owner's flip criterion of 2026-11-12 holds every point except the two 8x8/2if ones at or under 56 (`docs/design/SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY.md` section 5: "every SoC build is still refused past 56"). The assignment says an image over a **ledger entry** is not a stop: raise the entry. This image has no entry, so raising its limit means a new product exception and a change to the product build. No issue settles that.

**The images** (linked by `ctrl_srp_image.py` and `ctrl_plat_image.py` on one runtime and flash map; rom / sram bytes and planned RAMB36):

| Image | Base `16ba667d` | Head `def26a61` | Against its limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| platform 1x1/1if | 117,480 / 56,224, 43.0 | 119,648 / 56,224, 43.5 | within 56 |
| platform 8x8/1if | 130,184 / 97,328, **56.0** (888 B of rom spare) | 132,352 / 97,328, **56.5** | **over the 56 budget; refused** |
| platform 8x8/2if | 131,744 / 114,224, 60.5 (`ctrl_plat` 20,352 B) | 133,912 / 114,288, 61.0 (`ctrl_plat` 20,416 B) | over its entry of 60.5, the cap |
| size fixture 8x8/2if | 126,608 / 113,248, 59.0 | 128,784 / 113,248, 59.5 | over its entry of 59.0 |

Every other image stays within 56. The rom growth is the change's own code, 2,168 B at every platform point. In compiled text: `aecp_maps.c` +1,720 B (the command's commit 144 B; the boot commit of the restored maps, five functions, 1,124 B) and `aecp_face.c` +1,012 B (the `EDIT` window walk). A one-loop walk measured 216 B smaller. Even with the boot commit's refusal handling dropped as well, an estimated 1,270 B would remain, over the 888 B the image had spare. The command path alone, #923's first item, is an estimated 1,100 B. No compaction inside #923's scope returns the image to 56.0.

**Recommendation (A).** Ledger the target platform's 8x8/1if image at 56.5 RAMB36: half a tile, 1,280 B of rom owed to S14 (the move of cold code to flash, decision D3). The product SoC build would plan an image at its own ledgered point by its symbols, as the measurements already do by name. The memory tests, `plat_ledger.py` and section 5 would be updated with it. Under the assignment's rule, the two 8x8/2if entries are raised to their measured 59.5 and 61.0 (`ctrl_plat` 20,416 B), each half a tile of further S14 debt; the platform's goes past its 60.5 cap. (B) The alternative, the image held at 56.0, needs code moved out of the image, which is S14's work.

**State of the lane at `def26a61` (local; nothing pushed):**
- #923: an accepted ADD or REMOVE_AUDIO_MAPPINGS commits its changing mappings to the datapath's map store through the `EDIT` window before the core's map moves. It runs the release processor's transaction, and a store refusal is the command's answer. The restored maps reach the store when AECP opens. #924: SET_CONFIGURATION past configurations_count answers NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR, and SET_STREAM_INFO takes the 48-octet body. No RTL, mailbox contract or row bound changes.
- 14 new firmware unit tests and 29 planted defects, each caught by its named test on its words. The AECP app arm passes at one and two interfaces: 161 tests.
- Split co-simulation (`make -C tb/verilator/milan_dp twin-maps`, the platform firmware on the split datapath RTL): 21 checks pass. They cover an edited map reaching the render store, BAD_ARGUMENTS with the mappings in place, SUCCESS for 1, 2, 4 and 6 channels once they are removed, and a saved map restored at the next boot reaching the store. Its plant, the edit port cut (#923's defect), fails the store, format and edit checks by name.
- CPU budget harness, the edit groups: the largest legal command's record at 1x1/1if is 92,489 CPU cycles, 975 us by the rule, its stated 975 us unchanged. The one-row edit is 26,177 cycles, 275 us, under the paced class's 300 us, so no row moves. 0 budget misses and 0 passes over the share in those groups at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if. The full runs at both points, the answering-ports arm and the firmware campaigns are still running.
- The release image is byte-identical: `bios.bin` at both configs, base and head.
- The 1x1/1if split image is queued for its route. The 8x8/1if image cannot be built until this is decided: the product build refuses 56.5.

[A10] Ruling on the STOP (issuecomment-6906644789): **(A)**, under the owner's standing rule of 2026-11-15 10:27 that control-memory ROM may overflow for now as debt owed to S14.

- **8x8/1if platform image:** a new ledgered product entry at its measured 56.5 RAMB36, named S14 debt (cold code to flash, decision D3). Update the memory tests, the ledger script and section 5 of the fit page with it.

- **Not a licence to grow:** no compaction work in this lane, but any further growth in round 2 is reported per file, as here.
- **#924:** this PR closes it. The SET_STREAM_INFO bodies past 84 octets stay a stated limitation in the body; I will open a follow-up issue.
- Round 2 carries the running units' results while the firmware stays unchanged, as the STOP proposed.

Later lanes in the train (#920, #925 and the sync) apply the same rule: a measured overflow raises the entry and names the debt, with no STOP.

[A789] STOP (#923 and #924, round 2): the 1x1/1if split image misses the hold floor on all three of S9's directives, on one datapath path

**The gate.** Timing met: WNS and WHS at least +0.030 ns at every corner on the best of S9's three directives. 8x8/1if meets on all three. 1x1/1if meets setup on all three and the issue floor (WHS >= 0) everywhere, but its fast corners hold at +0.014 to +0.015 ns on every directive:

| Image | Directive | WNS / WHS, ns (worst corners) | Against +0.030 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x1/1if | ExtraPostPlacementOpt | +0.256 / +0.015 | hold under |
| 1x1/1if | ExtraTimingOpt | +0.126 / +0.014 | hold under |
| 1x1/1if | AltSpreadLogic_high | +0.195 / +0.014 | hold under |
| 8x8/1if | ExtraPostPlacementOpt | +0.295 / +0.036 | met |
| 8x8/1if | ExtraTimingOpt | +0.034 / +0.035 | met |
| 8x8/1if | AltSpreadLogic_high | +0.047 / +0.035 | met |
| 1x1/1if at the base `16ba667d` | ExtraPostPlacementOpt | +0.208 / +0.014 | hold under, the same path family |

**The path is not this lane's.** On every directive the one path under the floor is the same one inside `milan_datapath`: `g_tdm_render_live.g_master.chan_tdm_render/bank_r_reg[3][22]` to `u_fcdc/mem_r_reg_1/DIADI[22]`, a register into a RAMB36 data input, 0 logic levels, at both fast corners. That is the TDM render FIFO crossing that #919's ruling recorded as #927's (issuecomment-6907583837, item 1). The 1x1/1if export is the base's but for the control memory: one 2 KiB rom bank more (43.0 to 43.5 RAMB36) and the rom's contents. No RTL, constraint or generator input changed between `16ba667d` and the head. Routed at the base `16ba667d` on the recipe's directive, the 1x1/1if image misses the same way: +0.014 ns at both fast corners, on `chan_tdm_render/bank_r_reg[6][22]` to `u_fcdc/mem_r_reg_2/DIADI[22]`. So the miss is the base's.

**The question.** May this lane record its 1x1/1if routes as misses owed to #927, as #919's were, with no seeds and no further directives? Or must the 1x1/1if image meet the floor here? That needs a seed, a fourth directive or a logic cut in the datapath, and none of those is this lane's to choose. #927's acceptance names the 8x8/1if image and has 1x1/1if keep meeting, so no issue settles this one.

**Recommendation (A).** Record it as #927's: add the 1x1/1if TDM render FIFO crossing to #927's paths, and route again here only if the gateware changes.

**State of the lane at `70c100da` (local; nothing pushed):**
- #923 and #924 as round 1 left them, and the ruling's ledger: the 8x8/1if platform image at its own entry, 56.5 RAMB36, S14 debt; the 8x8/2if entries at 59.5 and 61.0. The product build plans a ledgered image at its own entry by its symbols. The 8x8/1if image routed at 56.5: 92.5 of the device's 135 Block RAM tiles, the fabric's 36. The 1x1/1if image: 82, the fabric's 38.5 (81 at the base). At the recipe's directive the 1x1/1if area moves by -74 LUT and -8 FF, and by one RAMB36: the 2 KiB rom bank the plan counts as a RAMB18 is placed as a RAMB36. The 8x8/1if base route, for its area delta, is running.
- Found and fixed this round:
  - The coverage ratchet: `aecp_maps.c` 418 of 419 branches. A test of a refused restore removal with a clipped reset set, and its plant, caught by name; the six changed files recorded at 100 %.
  - The harness at 8x8 with two interfaces: a TypeError from the product build's new `ledgered=`, and EDIT verdicts that read 0. Every edit there had answered NOT_SUPPORTED with no notice.
  - The firmware page's pin-control figure, 183 to 185, for the two twin-maps targets.
  - `rows_tiers.py` held at its module length.
- Costs, base to head, the same legs, by the rule: the one-row edit at 1x1/1if 255 to 295 us and the largest legal command 915 to 975 us, within the stated 300 and 975. At 8x8/2if 305 to 355 us and 1,325 to 1,395 us, within 595 and 1,650. The 8x8/2if one-row member is stated at 355 (325 before). No input of the tier model moves, so every row, the load, the pace and the slice stand.
- The full arm A at 1x1/1if, 93 groups, and the record classes over every held leg: RESULT PASS. Its only budget findings are the seven `backlog-owed` held-egress rows of the base, already ruled. The 8x8/1if parts report the same rows and the costs that shape takes past 1x1/1if's statements, as that point does.
- The release image is byte-identical (`bios.bin` at both configs).
- `twin-maps` at `70c100da`: its 20 checks pass, and its plant fails its three checks by name. Round 1's comment counted 21; the run has 20.
- The clean-clone workflow pass ran at `e628d35a`, before the figure fix. Every job passed but three:
  - The pin-control figure, now fixed.
  - The soc timing-cuts simulation and the publication census, killed by their 900 s wall clocks with the host at load 300 to 1,000. The timing-cuts rerun passed. The census's third run passed its 6 shapes (246 checks), but one of its 163 self-test arms was killed by the same clock, so it is unknown, not failed.
- At `70c100da` the pass is running again, on booked CPUs since the host restart, and its results go to the lane's handoff. No 4-shard sweep runs in this round: none runs beside a route or after a stop.

The census's third run passed its 6 shapes (246 checks), but one of its 163 self-test arms was killed by the same clock, so it is unknown, not failed.
  • At 70c100da the pass is running again, on booked CPUs since the host restart, and its results go to the lane's handoff. No 4-shard sweep runs in this round: none runs beside a route or after a stop.

[A10] Ruling on the round-2 STOP: (A). The 1x1/1if TDM render FIFO crossing is already in #927's scope (issuecomment-6908876362, which widened it to every split image at both shapes, this FIFO named). Record the 1x1/1if routes as "misses at the base, owed to #927", with your table and the base route. No seeds and no further directives. Route again only if gateware changes.

The rest of round 2 stands:

  • finish the 8x8/1if base route for the area delta;
  • run the remaining gates and the sweep;
  • post REVIEW READY.

Standing rule for every flip lane: a route miss on a path #927 names (the edit-claim enable, the AAF meter pair, the TDM render FIFO crossing, the mailbox register-read path and the record mover's host decode), reproduced at the lane's base, is owed to #927 and is not a STOP. Stop only for a miss on another path, or one the lane's change creates.

[A789] REVIEW READY (#923 and #924)
Commit: `70c100da` (branch `923-aecp-maps`, on `16ba667d`; local, the manager pushes)

Changed:
- #923: an accepted ADD or REMOVE_AUDIO_MAPPINGS commits the mappings that change the map to the datapath's map store through interface 0's `EDIT` window before the core's map moves, all or none (Milan v1.2 5.4.2.27, 5.4.2.28). A store refusal is the command's answer. The restored maps reach the store when AECP opens: each moved port's reset set leaves first, then each restored set joins it. Files: `aecp.h`, `aecp_maps.c`, `aecp_face.c`, `mbx.c`/`mbx.h`, `aecp_mbx.c`, `ctrl_app_aecp.c`.
- #924: SET_CONFIGURATION past configurations_count answers NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR (IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.7.1). SET_STREAM_INFO takes the 48-octet 2013 body (`aecp_commands.c`).
- Ruling (A) of issuecomment-6906679024:
  - `ctrl_memory.LEDGERED` gains the 8x8/1if platform entry at 56.5 RAMB36 (S14 debt). The 8x8/2if entries go to 59.5 and 61.0.
  - The product build plans a ledgered image at its own entry by its symbols (`own_point`, `add_ctrl_memory`).
  - The ledger tests, `plat_ledger.py` and the fit page's sections 3 and 5 follow.
- Tests:
  - 14 GoogleTest cases and 30 planted defects, each caught by its named test.
  - `twin-maps` and `twin-maps-plants` on the split RTL.
  - The coverage ratchet records the six changed files at 100 %.
- Harness (`split_soc.py`): `EDIT` answered at the contract's bound. Its verdicts are a constant on the port; at two interfaces they had read 0. The 8x8 two-interface plan holds its named point over the build's.
- Stated costs by the rule (`edit_rows.PACED`): the one-row edit is 295 us at 1x1/1if and 355 at 8x8/2if. No tier input moves. Section 13 and FR_NFR carry the base-to-head figures.

Validation (clean clones of `70c100da` unless named):
- Workflow jobs of `rtl-fast.yml`, `elaborate.yml` and `docs.yml`, step by step (`verify_wf.py`): 118 steps rc 0, 130 not run with their reasons, 0 bad, among them the AECP (329 of 329), SRP (421 of 421) and control (716 of 716) campaigns, `fw_coverage.py --check` (PASS, 39 files), the publication census and `ctrl_boundary.py`.
- Native 4-shard sweep (`scripts/run_all_suites.sh --wait --shard k/4`): every shard exit 0: 65 suites PASS, 2,713,040 checks, 0 failures, none timed out.
- `twin-maps`: 20 checks PASS. `twin-maps-plants`: the no-edit plant fails its 3 checks by name.
- CPU budget harness, full arm A at 1x1/1if (93 groups) and 8x8/1if (93, reported), and the edit legs of arm B. Firmware as at `def26a61`; the harness's later change is a no-op at one interface.
  - 0 refusals and no pass over THE SHARE at 1x1/1if.
  - The only budget misses are the seven `backlog-owed` held-egress rows, the base's and already ruled.
  - `record_classes.py` over every leg at both points: RESULT PASS (long 975/975, paced 295/300, ordinary 210/235 us at 1x1/1if).
  - `rows_tiers.py` prints the base's table; `load_grade.py --check` and `flip_grade.py --check --point 1x1/1if` PASS.
- Costs, base `16ba667d` to head, same legs:
  - 1x1/1if: one-row edit 23,877 to 27,866 cycles (295 us); largest legal command 86,698 to 92,714 (975, stated 975).
  - 8x8/2if: 28,627 to 33,481 (355); 126,152 to 132,751 (1,395, stated 1,650).
- Release image: `bios.bin` byte-identical at both configs (`679b4a44`; nothing it reads changed after).
- S9 split images, six head routes and two base routes at ExtraPostPlacementOpt:
  - 8x8/1if meets WNS and WHS >= +0.030 ns on all three directives (best +0.295 / +0.036). The base misses setup at +0.011 on #927's edit-claim enable.
  - 1x1/1if misses hold on all three (+0.015 / +0.014 / +0.014) on the TDM render FIFO crossing, as its base does (+0.014). Recorded as misses at the base, owed to #927 (ruling issuecomment-6923091710).
- Device and area:
  - 1x1/1if: 82 of 135 Block RAM tiles (base 81). LUT -74, FF -8, one RAMB36: the plan's RAMB18 for the new 2 KiB rom bank is placed as a RAMB36.
  - 8x8/1if: 92.5 tiles at both. LUT +52, FF +36.

Acceptance criteria:
- #923: met.
  - The edit and the restore reach the render store on the split RTL (twin-maps).
  - GET_AUDIO_MAP agrees after every command.
  - BAD_ARGUMENTS with the mappings in place, SUCCESS for 1, 2, 4 and 6 channels once they are removed.
  - Each check has a planted defect caught by name; branch coverage of the new code is 100 %.
- #924: met. Tested and planted; the 48-octet body is answered in the 84-octet form.

Open risks/questions:
- SET_STREAM_INFO bodies past 84 octets are still taken: #926.
- The 1x1/1if hold miss is #927's.
- Round 1's STOP counted 21 twin-maps checks; it is 20.
